title: DROP FUNCTION
description: DROP FUNCTION removes a function definition - Postgres needs the parameter types too, since two functions can share a name if their parameter types differ. The fixtures already include a function `full_name(first_name TEXT, last_name TEXT)` - drop it.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: DROP FUNCTION
DROP FUNCTION <name>(<param_type>, <param_type>) - unlike DROP TABLE or DROP VIEW, you have to repeat the parameter types so Postgres knows exactly which overload you mean.
Use DROP FUNCTION followed by full_name and the exact parameter types (TEXT, TEXT) in parentheses.
expected_behavior: full_name(TEXT, TEXT) no longer exists as a function.
explanation: Postgres allows function overloading (the same name with different parameter types counts as different functions), which is exactly why DROP FUNCTION needs the full signature, not just the name.
